newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - July 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - July 28.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- State-owned businesses in Nanchang, eastern Jiangxi province, deepen reform to meet requirements of socialist market economy.
- Commentary calls for deepening reform of state-owned businesses with companies urged to make progress despite difficulties.
- Six million mu of cotton in Jiangsu province is in good condition
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH
- Farmers in southern Guangdong province make profits by means of advanced agricultural sciences and technologies.
- Chinese frontier guards enhance unity between army and frontier inhabitants, promoting economic development and social stability.
CHINA SECURITIES
- Economist Gao Shangquan says reform of industry needs to nurture private sector and develop capital market
- Ministry of Railways to reduced 60,000 staff a year from 1997 to 2000
FINANCIAL NEWS
- Output of cars is expected at 7.5 million in 1997, down 10-15 percent from last year
CHINA BUSINESS DAILY
- Laid off workers in China reach 10 million in first half
INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS DAILY
- By end-1996, U.S. investment in China reached $14.3 billion
MARKET DAILY
- Central government decides Chongqing to have same favourable policy as Pudong
CHINA DAILY
- China establishes ties with Cook Islands
- Citic Chairman Wang Jun denies paying for meeting with U.S. President Bill Clinton
